title: SpecCloak: Probing Harmful Code Generation through Engineering Specifications
title_zh: SpecCloak：通过工程规范探究有害代码生成

paragraphs.en: SpecCloak 通过工程规范研究大型语言模型在代码生成中的安全行为，并提出了一种黑盒红队测试框架。 The code generation capabilities of large language models (LLMs) can equally be misused to implement harmful functionality, underscoring the need to understand their safety behavior in response to programming requests. While request phrasing is known to influence refusal, it remains unclear whether the form in which coding task requirements are stated affects the refusal process for malicious code generation. We introduce PseudoSpec, a template that organizes functional requirements as engineering specifications, and investigate its effects through controlled comparisons, representation analysis, and activation interventions. Across five open-weight models, removing explicit risk keywords only partially reduces refusal, whereas specification prompting substantially lowers refusal even when these keywords are retained. This reduction accompanies consistent shifts toward code-output-related representations, and interventions along condition-difference directions alter refusal behavior. Output analysis further distinguishes code-related responses from generation degeneration. Building on these findings, we propose SpecCloak, a black-box red-teaming framework combining PseudoSpec with discriminator-guided optimization, achieving an average execution-verified attack success rate of 28.91\% across eight target models on RedCode-Gen. We also introduce SpecReveal, a defense prototype combining natural-language intent reconstruction with dual-view detection without target-model fine-tuning. It achieves a 96.88\% attack detection rate in a separate prompt-detection evaluation, with false positives assessed on benign programming and specification-style inputs. These results connect specification-induced response differences to practical security consequences and identify intent reconstruction as a complementary detection approach.
paragraphs.zh: SpecCloak 通过工程规范研究大型语言模型在代码生成中的安全行为，并提出了一种黑盒红队测试框架。大型语言模型（LLM）的代码生成能力同样可能被滥用以实现有害功能，这凸显了理解其在响应编程请求时的安全行为的必要性。 尽管已知请求的措辞会影响拒绝行为，但目前尚不清楚编码任务要求的表述形式是否会影响恶意代码生成的拒绝过程。 我们引入了 PseudoSpec，这是一种将功能需求组织为工程规范的模板，并通过受控比较、表示分析和激活干预来研究其效果。 在五个开放权重模型中，移除明确的风险关键词仅能部分减少拒绝行为，而规范提示即使保留这些关键词也能显著降低拒绝率。 这种降低伴随着向代码输出相关表示的一致性转变，而沿条件差异方向进行的干预会改变拒绝行为。 输出分析进一步区分了与代码相关的响应和生成退化现象。 基于这些发现，我们提出了 SpecCloak，一种结合 PseudoSpec 与判别器引导优化的黑盒红队测试框架，在 RedCode-Gen 上的八个目标模型中实现了平均 28.91\% 的执行验证攻击成功率。 我们还引入了 SpecReveal，一种无需对目标模型进行微调的防御原型，它结合了自然语言意图重建与双视角检测。 在独立的提示检测评估中，该原型实现了 96.88\% 的攻击检测率，其误报率则通过良性编程和风格为规范的输入进行评估。 这些结果将规范引发的响应差异与实际安全后果联系起来，并指出意图重建是一种互补的检测方法。
